newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chile launches search for Canadian yachtsman.
newsitem.headline: Chile launches search for Canadian yachtsman.

text.p: Chile on Friday launched a search for missing lone Canadian yachtsman Gerry Roufs after a military plane reported radio contact with Rouf's yacht near Cape Horn, organisers of the Vendee Globe round-the-world race said.
They said the pilot of the Chilean aircraft made brief radio contact late on Thursday with the yacht which has been missing for 10 days, but bad weather prevented him from seeing it.
Chief race organiser Philippe Jeantot voiced caution however, saying there could be confusion about the name of the yacht, Group LG2.
"I would like to believe the report. It would be fabulous. But an error on the name of the boat is possible," he told French radio and television.
He said the Chilean military had despatched more planes and helicopters to confirm the sighting.
The French maritime rescue service Cross-Etel, which is coordinating the search for Roufs, said the yacht gave its name and position to the Chilean plane a few miles from Cape Horn.
"The report is to be treated with caution and needs to be confirmed," it said in a statement.
Jeantot said the report would soon be confirmed or denied as the yacht was about to round Cape Horn where the Chilean military had tracking facilities.

The Paris headquarters of the race lost track of the Canadian's automatic satellite location beacon 10 days ago somewhere between New Zealand, South America and Antarctica, in an area some 2,500 miles west of Cape Horn.

Organisers have said Roufs had not set off distress signals, meaning either that he was sailing normally without being able to make contact, or his yacht had capsized and he had not been able to raise the alert.
Searches by two freighters and a Canadian satellite have failed to turn up any sign of the missing yachtsman, who was skirting Antarctica eastwards.
Two other race competitors, Frenchman Thierry Dubois and Briton Tony Bullimore, were rescued by the Australian navy after their boats capsized southwest of Australia.
